🌱 Basics · Lesson 1 · 2 min read

What is AI?

What artificial intelligence really is — and what it isn't.

A simple definition

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the ability of a computer system to do tasks that usually need human intelligence: recognising faces, understanding speech, translating languages or making decisions. AI doesn't think like a person. It finds patterns in data and uses them to make predictions — like guessing which word you'll type next.

Did you know? The term “artificial intelligence” was invented in 1955 by computer scientist John McCarthy, for a summer workshop at Dartmouth College in 1956. So AI is older than the Internet!

Rules vs. learning

Classic programs follow rules that a programmer writes by hand: “if the temperature is below 0 °C, show a snowflake”. Most modern AI works differently: it learns its own rules from examples. Instead of describing what a cat looks like, you show the computer thousands of cat photos, and it figures out the pattern by itself.

Did you know? Nobody tells a spam filter every trick that scammers use. It learns to spot new tricks from millions of emails that people marked as spam.

Narrow AI vs. general AI

Today's AI is narrow: each system is built for a certain kind of task. A chess program can beat any human champion, but it can't recognise a cat. Even chatbots that can talk about almost anything still make mistakes that a child wouldn't. Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) — an AI that could learn any intellectual task a human can — doesn't exist yet, and experts disagree about when, or whether, it will arrive.

Why it matters to you

AI already decides which videos you see, makes your photos look better and helps doctors find diseases. Knowing the basics helps you use it wisely, notice its mistakes — and maybe one day build AI yourself.

Key points

  • AI means computer systems doing tasks that normally need human intelligence.
  • Modern AI learns patterns from data instead of only following hand-written rules.
  • All AI today is limited: human-level general AI (AGI) doesn't exist yet.

Check yourself

Which of these is the best example of AI?

Show the answer

Right answer: A translation app that learned from millions of translated texts

The translation app learned patterns from huge amounts of data. The lamp and the alarm clock just follow simple, fixed rules — no learning involved.
